#### [There's no place like home...](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0037059/reviews/?featured=rw4772403&ref_=tt_ururv_c_5_hd)

I suspect I didn't give "Meet Me in St. Louis" the attention it fully deserved.  
  
Sometimes, the words Technicolor, musical, Golden Age don't necessarily hit a sensitive chord and I blame it on the Millennial side of me, too blasé and hungry of modern significance. I could watch "The Wizard of Oz" for its status as an iconic classic, "A Star is Born" for its relevance and place in Judy Garland's filmography. But Vincente Minnelli's ode to Saint Louis never caught my attention despite its more than respectable reputation. And now that I saw it, and that I digested it, I realize how misinformed I was and I suspect this is a film I might want to watch again.  
  
This is one of these pitch-proof movie where you keep waiting for something to happen... yet you realize that's not even the point. Indeed, who needs plot when you have the Smithes? This is a family full of such colorful characters that there's no room whatsoever for any plot or pre-written arc. Why should it anyway? Adapted from the happy memories of Sally "Tootie" Benson (yes, told from the little one's standpoint), the film displays such an exhilarating form of happiness that spoiling it with a plot would be a cinematic sin.  
  
So let's visit the family! Leon Ames is Mr. Smith, father of one son and four daughters including Rose (Lucille Bremer), the second oldest Esther (Judy Garland) and the youngest one, Tootie (Margaret O'Brien), Mrs. Smith (Mary Astor) endure their shenanigans valiantly while they can count on the support of their cool and hilarious grandpa (Henry Davenport). These are the Smiths and as soon as they appear on the screen, we're literally caught in their communicative amiability and optimism with the opening theme of the same title.  
  
"Meet Me in Saint Louis" belongs to these vignette family-themed movies such as "Amarcord" or "Radio Days" where it's just about getting a mood and feeling part of a loving community rather than watching something happening. And just when you think something ought to happen, false alarm, a new song pops up again to lift your spirit up and puts you in the most cheerful mood, even the "straight" sister Rose is fun to watch, especially during her shining moment where she gets quite a brush from her correspondent. And everything's in good spirit, no character is laughed at but rather laughed with.  
  
The closest to a plot comes when Mr. Smith announces to the family that they're going to move to New York and the decision is irrevocable, by the time it happens, we got used to the seasonal enchantment of the city and can't imagine the Smiths anywhere outside St. Louis. Even New York resonates like a place of doom for the family, but it's deliberate since the film is a postcard recollection of middle-upper class family, from the perspective of Tootie, only spiced up with adult and romantic subplot and unforgettable musical numbers that were the perfect vehicles for Judy Garland.  
  
If "Meet Me in Saint Louis" is incredibly catchy, it's nothing compared to the "Trolley Song" and of course the "Have Yourself a merry Little Christmas" that became Hollywood standards and among Garland's signatures. The two songs, listed in the AFI's Top 100, convey two opposite emotions: joy and sheer sadness, the excitement of being part of a city and the resignation before living, the Christmas moment is particularly heartbreaking as it allows Margaret O'Brien to implode her full acting power and make thousands of souls cry with empathetic tears. That the comic relief of the film, that bratty little kid could pull off such a masterful performance is one of the unexpected effects of the film. She would deservedly win an Academy Juvenile Award for her incredible performance.  
  
I can go over and over about the film, its merit is to be so blatantly cheerful, never indulging to cheap thrills, even the love stories are sweetly naïve and idealistic, almost surreal but fitting for a fantasy picture whose purpose is to highlight the real thing about th film: family ties, and the bonds between sisters or parents and grandparents, the film is a non-stop delight, that can be regarded as itsch or campy but I find it more straightforward and honest than Minnelli' "An American in Paris". In a way, it's a fine companion piece to Judy Garland's Wizard of Oz with the same conclusion that there's no place like home... and sometimes, we don't cherish enough the place we live in.  
  
My only complaint is Garland's awful hairstyle, was she trying to imitate Katharine Hepburn or what?

**David Yates** (born 8 October 1963) is an English filmmaker, who has directed feature films, short films, and television productions. He is best known for directing the final four films in the [_Harry Potter_ series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry_Potter_(film_series) "Harry Potter (film series)") and the three films of its prequel series, _[Fantastic Beasts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fantastic\_Beasts\_(film\_series) "Fantastic Beasts (film series)")_.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-DGA-DavidYatesDirectorProfile-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-BAFTABritannia-4) His work on the _Harry Potter_ series brought him critical and commercial success along with accolades, such as the [British Academy Britannia Award for Excellence in Directing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Britannia_Awards "Britannia Awards").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-BAFTABritannia-4)

Yates directed various short films and became a television director early in his career. His credits include the six-part political thriller _[State of Play](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State\_of\_Play\_(TV\_serial) "State of Play (TV serial)")_ (2003), for which he won the [Directors Guild of Great Britain Award for Outstanding Directorial Achievement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Directors_Guild_of_Great_Britain "Directors Guild of Great Britain"), the adult two-part documentary drama _[Sex Traffic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sex\_Traffic "Sex Traffic")_ (2004) and the [Emmy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emmy_Award "Emmy Award")-winning television film _[The Girl in the Café](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Girl\_in\_the\_Caf%C3%A9 "The Girl in the Café")_ (2005).[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-DGA-DavidYatesDirectorProfile-3)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-DavidYatesDoesItAll-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-VirginMedia-DavidYates-6)

Yates is a founding member of [Directors UK](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Directors_UK "Directors UK"),[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-7) and has had a close partnership with [Warner Bros.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Bros. "Warner Bros.") as a director and producer.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-8) Around 2022 he started work out of his own production company, Wychwood Media.

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=David_Yates&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

David was born on 8 October 1963 in [St Helens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St_Helens,_Merseyside "St Helens, Merseyside"), England. He was raised in the village of [Rainhill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rainhill "Rainhill"). His parents died when he was young.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-DavidYatesCollider2011-9) Yates was inspired to pursue a career in filmmaking after watching [Steven Spielberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Spielberg "Steven Spielberg")'s 1975 movie _[Jaws](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaws\_(film) "Jaws (film)")_.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-DavidYatesEarlyLifeBAFTA-1) Yates's mother bought him a [Super 8mm camera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_8_film_cameras "Super 8 film cameras"). He used this to shoot various films in which his friends and family featured.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-FilmLondon-DavidYates-10) One such film, _The Ghost Ship_, was shot on board the vessel where his uncle worked as a cook.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-11) He attended Grange Park High School,[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-Star-12)[St Helens College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St_Helens_College "St Helens College") and then the [University of Essex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Essex "University of Essex").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-Yahoo!Movies-DavidYatesBio-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-David_Yates_Casarotto-15) Yates said that he "used to skive off college all the time" and never expected to attend university before being surprised by his A-Level exam results. While at the University of Essex, Yates formed the Film and Video Production Society.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-16) He graduated with a [BA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Arts "Bachelor of Arts") in Government in 1987.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-17)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=David_Yates&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

### Television and film career (1988–2005)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=David_Yates&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Television and film career (1988–2005)")]

[![Image 19](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/82/BeaconsfieldFilmStudios.jpg/250px-BeaconsfieldFilmStudios.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:BeaconsfieldFilmStudios.jpg)

The [National Film and Television School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_and_Television_School "National Film and Television School"), where Yates trained as a director[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-18)

In 1988, Yates made his first film _When I Was a Girl_ in [Swindon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swindon "Swindon"). The film entered the festival circuit where it was named [Best Short Film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco_International_Film_Festival#Golden_Gate_Awards "San Francisco International Film Festival") at the [San Francisco International Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco_International_Film_Festival "San Francisco International Film Festival"). It contributed towards Yates's acceptance into the [National Film and Television School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_and_Television_School "National Film and Television School") in 1989 and led to the [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC "BBC") hiring him to direct _Oranges and Lemons_, a short drama film in 1991. Before completing film school, he began to direct, produce and write the screenplay to the dramatic short _The Weaver's Wife_. He also made his fourth short film, _Good Looks_, which was presented at the [Chicago International Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_International_Film_Festival "Chicago International Film Festival"). After graduating in 1992, Yates directed an episode of the film studies programme _[Moving Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moving\_Pictures\_(TV\_series) "Moving Pictures (TV series)")_.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-FilmLondon-DavidYates-10)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-Yahoo!Movies-DavidYatesBio-13)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-NFTS-DavidYatesCourses-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-DirectorandComposerCollaborations-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-22)

From 1994 to 1995, Yates directed several episodes of the [ITV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ITV_(TV_network) "ITV (TV network)") police procedural _[The Bill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Bill "The Bill")_ before directing and producing three episodes of the television documentary _Tale of Three Seaside Towns_ alongside producer Alistair Clarke. The programme followed media personalities [Russell Grant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russell_Grant "Russell Grant"), [Honor Blackman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honor_Blackman "Honor Blackman") and [Pam Ayres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pam_Ayres "Pam Ayres") visiting and exploring the [South Coast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_England "Southern England") towns of [Brighton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brighton "Brighton"), [Eastbourne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastbourne "Eastbourne") and [Weymouth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weymouth,_Dorset "Weymouth, Dorset").[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-24) Yates directed his fifth short film _Punch_ before making his feature film debut in 1998 with the release of the independent historical-drama film _[The Tichborne Claimant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Tichborne\_Claimant\_(film) "The Tichborne Claimant (film)")_. The film, which was shown at the [Edinburgh International Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edinburgh_International_Film_Festival "Edinburgh International Film Festival"), was written by Joe Fisher and based on the true events of the [Tichborne Case](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tichborne_Case "Tichborne Case"). It starred [Stephen Fry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Fry "Stephen Fry") and [Robert Hardy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Hardy "Robert Hardy") and was shot on location in [Merseyside](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Merseyside "Merseyside") and on the [Isle of Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isle_of_Man "Isle of Man").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-27)

Yates returned to television in 2000 to direct the episodes of _Greed_, _Envy_ and _Lust_ for the BBC miniseries _[The Sins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Sins "The Sins")_, starring [Pete Postlethwaite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pete_Postlethwaite "Pete Postlethwaite"), as well as _[The Way We Live Now](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Way\_We\_Live\_Now\_(2001\_TV\_serial) "The Way We Live Now (2001 TV serial)")_, the four-part television adaptation of the [novel of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Way_We_Live_Now "The Way We Live Now") by [Anthony Trollope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Trollope "Anthony Trollope"). Yates shared the [British Academy Television Award for Best Drama Serial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Academy_Television_Awards#Categories "British Academy Television Awards") with screenwriter [Andrew Davies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Davies_(writer) "Andrew Davies (writer)") and producer [Nigel Stafford-Clark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigel_Stafford-Clark "Nigel Stafford-Clark") at the [2002 BAFTA Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Academy_Television_Awards_2002 "British Academy Television Awards 2002").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-28)

One year later, Yates attended the [56th BAFTA Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/56th_British_Academy_Film_Awards "56th British Academy Film Awards") with a [British Academy Film Award nomination for Best Short Film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Best_Short_Film "BAFTA Award for Best Short Film") for the fourteen-minute production, _[Rank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rank\_(film) "Rank (film)")_, which expressed the social elements of racism, friendship and adolescence through the story of a street gang that cross [Glasgow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glasgow "Glasgow") to witness the arrival of a group of Somali refugees.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-30) Yates said that even though _The Way We Live Now_ was "a very big production" and "enormous fun to do", _Rank_ was an opportunity to "shake all that off" and "get back to [his] roots". Of the casting, Yates said that he "wanted to use non-actors to tell the story, to create a reality ... the kids we cast in Glasgow had never done a film before."[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-FilmLondon-DavidYates-10) The film was noted for its gritty style and cinematography, with a review from _Eye For Film_ stating that "such intelligent use of camera and cast lifts Yates out of the pool of promising young directors into the front line of genuine hopefuls. This work demands respect."[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-NFTS-DavidYatesCourses-19)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-31)

The 2003 six-part thriller _[State of Play](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State\_of\_Play\_(TV\_serial) "State of Play (TV serial)")_ was Yates's next achievement.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-DavidYatesDoesItAll-5) Yates collected the TV Spielfilm Award at the [Cologne Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cologne_Conference "Cologne Conference") in Germany and won the [Directors Guild of Great Britain Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Directors_Guild_of_Great_Britain "Directors Guild of Great Britain") for Outstanding Directorial Achievement.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-DGA-DavidYatesDirectorProfile-3)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-32) The serial was recognised by various award ceremonies, receiving the [Peabody Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peabody_Award "Peabody Award") for Broadcasting Excellence and being presented with two [British Academy Television Craft Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Academy_Television_Craft_Awards "British Academy Television Craft Awards").[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-33) The quality of the serial sparked Hollywood film bosses to consider [adapting it into a film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_of_Play_(film) "State of Play (film)"), with producer [Andrew Hauptman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Hauptman "Andrew Hauptman") declaring that "it's a blistering political thriller and we want to make an equally blistering movie."[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-34)_State of Play_ is regarded by critics from _[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Guardian "The Guardian")_ and _[The Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Times "The Times")_ as one of the best British television dramas of the 2000s.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-35)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-36)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-37)

Yates directed the television adaptation of nine-year-old [Daisy Ashford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daisy_Ashford "Daisy Ashford")'s novel _[The Young Visiters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Young\_Visiters#Adaptations "The Young Visiters")_, starring [Jim Broadbent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Broadbent "Jim Broadbent") alongside [Hugh Laurie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hugh_Laurie "Hugh Laurie"). According to a review by [_Variety_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variety_(magazine) "Variety (magazine)") magazine for [BBC America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_America "BBC America"), Yates and his team yielded "a warm and surprisingly unsentimental production that has 'evergreen' written all over it".[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-38)

In 2004, Yates's two-part drama _[Sex Traffic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sex\_Traffic "Sex Traffic")_ was broadcast on [Channel 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channel_4 "Channel 4"). It won eight BAFTA Awards including [Best Editing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Best_Editing "BAFTA Award for Best Editing") for [Mark Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Day_(film_editor) "Mark Day (film editor)"), who regularly worked with Yates on many of his television projects and short films. Day commented on his collaboration with Yates saying that "we are very good friends because we have spent so much time together". He also said, "David shoots in a similar style from piece to piece, although this wasn’t quite as frantic as _State of Play_."[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-EditorWinsBAFTA-39) Yates was nominated for another Directors Guild of Great Britain Award for his direction of _Sex Traffic_ and won his second BAFTA for Best Drama Serial at the British Academy Television Awards.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-40) Being a British-Canadian production, _Sex Traffic_ gained four wins at Canada's annual television award ceremony, the [Gemini Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gemini_Award "Gemini Award"), including Best Dramatic Miniseries. Spanning across two parts, the three-hour-long drama reveals how the [trafficking of young women](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_trafficking "Human trafficking") into slavery is a big business which operates throughout Europe; both parts were acclaimed for their "shocking" portrayal of such a sensitive topic.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-41)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-42)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-43)

Also in 2004, Yates was involved in plans for a film adaptation of [Evelyn Waugh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evelyn_Waugh "Evelyn Waugh")'s novel _[Brideshead Revisited](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brideshead\_Revisited "Brideshead Revisited")_ for [Warner Independent Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Independent_Pictures "Warner Independent Pictures"). He was set to work with [Paul Bettany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Bettany "Paul Bettany"), [Jude Law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jude_Law "Jude Law") and [Jennifer Connelly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jennifer_Connelly "Jennifer Connelly") on the project, but pulled out in the later stages due to constant budget issues affecting the film's production.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-DarkHorizons-DavidYatesBridesheadRevisited&HBP-44)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-VarietyReviewsBrideshead-45)

Yates then directed [Richard Curtis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Curtis "Richard Curtis")' script to _[The Girl in the Café](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Girl\_in\_the\_Caf%C3%A9 "The Girl in the Café")_, a television film starring [Bill Nighy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Nighy "Bill Nighy") and [Kelly Macdonald](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kelly_Macdonald "Kelly Macdonald"). In June 2005, the film was aired on the BBC in Britain and was also broadcast in the United States on [Home Box Office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HBO "HBO"). _The Girl in the Café_ achieved three wins at the [Emmy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Award "Primetime Emmy Award"), including the [Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Made for Television Movie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Award_for_Outstanding_Made_for_Television_Movie "Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Made for Television Movie"), and gained a total of four nominations including [Outstanding Directing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Award_for_Outstanding_Directing_for_a_Miniseries,_Movie_or_a_Dramatic_Special "Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Directing for a Miniseries, Movie or a Dramatic Special") for Yates.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-Yahoo!Movies-DavidYatesBio-13)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-46)[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-47)

### _Harry Potter_ (2006–2011)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=David_Yates&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Harry Potter (2006–2011)")]

[![Image 20](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5b/David_Yates.jpg/250px-David_Yates.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:David_Yates.jpg)

Yates outside [Grauman's Chinese Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grauman's_Chinese_Theatre "Grauman's Chinese Theatre") at the premiere of _[Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry\_Potter\_and\_the\_Order\_of\_the\_Phoenix\_(film) "Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (film)")_ on 8 July 2007

During the period of working on plans for _Brideshead Revisited_, Yates was told by his agent that he had made the director shortlist for the fifth film in the [_Harry Potter_ series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry_Potter_(film_series) "Harry Potter (film series)") and that Warner Bros. was eyeing him to direct. Shortly after, he was confirmed to direct _[Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry\_Potter\_and\_the\_Order\_of\_the\_Phoenix\_(film) "Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (film)")_ by [Warner Bros. Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Bros._Pictures "Warner Bros. Pictures"), with production scheduled to begin in early 2006.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-VarietyReviewsBrideshead-45)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-48) When asked how Yates got the job, producer [David Heyman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Heyman "David Heyman") ("a big fan" of Yates's television work)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-TheObserver-DavidYatesinterview-49) said that "actors in David's television projects give their best performance, often of their career. It's important to keep pushing the actors, particularly the young ones on each _Potter_ film. This is a political film, not with a capital P, but it's about teen rebellion and the abuse of power. David has made films in the U.K. about politics without being heavy handed."[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-HeymanYatesOOTP-50)

Before production began, Yates invited _[Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry\_Potter\_and\_the\_Goblet\_of\_Fire\_(film) "Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire (film)")_ director [Mike Newell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Newell_(director) "Mike Newell (director)") to a pub and "picked his brains about what it was going to be like to step into someone's shoes on a movie of this scale".[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-DGA-DavidYatesDirectorProfile-3) The first scene that Yates shot featured a [giant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giant "Giant") interacting with human characters. The scene was the very first high-scale [visual effects](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visual_effects "Visual effects") piece Yates filmed in his career.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-DGA-DavidYatesDirectorProfile-3)[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-51) After the film's post-production material was well received by the studio, Yates was chosen to direct the sixth film, _[Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry\_Potter\_and\_the\_Half-Blood\_Prince\_(film) "Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (film)")_, which according to Yates was going to be "a cross between the chills of _[Prisoner of Azkaban](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry\_Potter\_and\_the\_Prisoner\_of\_Azkaban\_(film) "Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban (film)")_ [the third film in the series] and the fantastical adventure of _Goblet of Fire_".[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-VirginMedia-DavidYates-6)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-DarkHorizons-DavidYatesBridesheadRevisited&HBP-44)

In 2007, _Order of the Phoenix_ opened to positive reviews and commercial success. Yates won the title of [Best Director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Empire_Award_for_Best_Director "Empire Award for Best Director") at the [Empire Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Empire_Awards "Empire Awards") and collected the [People's Choice Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Film_Academy_People's_Choice_Award_for_Best_European_Film "European Film Academy People's Choice Award for Best European Film") from the [European Film Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Film_Academy "European Film Academy").[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-52) However, the film was criticised by fans of the series for having the shortest running time out of the five released instalments; Yates said that the original director's cut was "probably over three hours", resulting in much footage being cut, condensed and edited to fit within the studio's preferred time frame.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-53)[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-54)

During production of _Half-Blood Prince_, Warner Bros. executive [Alan F. Horn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_F._Horn "Alan F. Horn") announced that the seventh and final novel in the series, _[Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry\_Potter\_and\_the\_Deathly\_Hallows "Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows")_, was to be split into two cinematic parts with Yates, once again, as the director.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-55) Yates spoke of the decision to appoint him as the director of the final films, remarking that "they wanted to do a _Harry Potter_ that felt ... more grown up. What's smart about the studio and the producers is they have always wanted to push it a bit. [Chris Columbus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Columbus_(filmmaker) "Chris Columbus (filmmaker)") did a wonderful job of casting and making this world incredibly popular. But rather than do more of the same, they said, 'Let's bring in [Alfonso Cuarón](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfonso_Cuar%C3%B3n "Alfonso Cuarón") and let him run with it. Then later, let's bring in David Yates, who's done all this hard-hitting stuff on TV.' It's a testament to their ambition to try to keep the franchise fresh. The bizarre thing is, I did one [film] and they asked me to stay for three more, so obviously they liked something."[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-DGA-DavidYatesDirectorProfile-3)

_Half-Blood Prince_ was released in 2009 and became the only film in the series to earn an [Academy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards") nomination for [Best Cinematography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Cinematography "Academy Award for Best Cinematography").[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-56)[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-57) Yates worked alongside French cinematographer [Bruno Delbonnel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruno_Delbonnel "Bruno Delbonnel") on, what Yates called, extensively colour grading the "incredibly rich" picture by making it look "very European" and drawing influences from the Dutch painter [Rembrandt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rembrandt "Rembrandt").[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-58)[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-59)[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-60) The film garnered a mix of accolades and was acclaimed for its stylised character-driven approach, but some fans complained about the script's deviation from the novel and the film's slight [romantic comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romantic_comedy "Romantic comedy") nature.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-61) In response to this criticism, BAFTA member and film critic [Mark Kermode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Kermode "Mark Kermode") praised Yates's direction and ranked the film "second best" in the series, behind _Prisoner of Azkaban_.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-62)

Yates [began to film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Production_of_Harry_Potter_and_the_Deathly_Hallows "Production of Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows")_[Deathly Hallows – Part 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry\_Potter\_and\_the\_Deathly\_Hallows\_%E2%80%93\_Part\_1 "Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows – Part 1")_ and _[Deathly Hallows – Part 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry\_Potter\_and\_the\_Deathly\_Hallows\_%E2%80%93\_Part\_2 "Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows – Part 2")_ back-to-back in early 2009 and finished reshoots in late 2010.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-63) He stated that he had shot the two parts of the final adaptation differently, with Part 1 being a "[road movie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Road_movie "Road movie")" and "quite real", "almost like a [vérité](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cin%C3%A9ma_v%C3%A9rit%C3%A9 "Cinéma vérité") documentary", while Part 2 is "more operatic, colourful and [fantasy-oriented](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fantasy_film "Fantasy film")", a "big opera with huge battles."[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-64)[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-65)[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-66) Yates reshot the final scene of the _Harry Potter_ series at [Leavesden Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Bros._Studios_Leavesden "Warner Bros. Studios Leavesden") after the original version, filmed at [London King's Cross railway station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_King's_Cross_railway_station "London King's Cross railway station"), did not meet his expectations. In the film, the scene takes place at the magical [Platform 9¾](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Platform_9%C2%BE "Platform 9¾").[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-67)

Part 1 was released worldwide in November 2010 to commercial success along with generally positive reviews, some of which reflected on Yates's directing style. _[The Dallas Morning News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Dallas\_Morning\_News "The Dallas Morning News")_ affirmed that "David Yates' fluid, fast-paced direction sends up the crackling tension of a thriller" and _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_York\_Times "The New York Times")_ analysed Yates's approach to J. K. Rowling's character development by saying that he has "demonstrated a thorough, uncondescending sympathy for her characters, in particular the central trio of [Ron Weasley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ron_Weasley "Ron Weasley"), [Hermione Granger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hermione_Granger "Hermione Granger") and [Harry Potter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry_Potter_(character) "Harry Potter (character)") himself."[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-68)[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-69) The film was praised for its "dark" atmosphere and its loyalty to the source material, but it was criticised for its slow middle act, the handling of exposition, and the somewhat disjointed pacing.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-70)[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-71)

Part 2 was screened in July 2011 and became an instant record-breaking success with critical acclaim.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-DH2RT-72)[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-DH2MC-73)_[The Daily Telegraph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Daily\_Telegraph "The Daily Telegraph")_ described Part 2 as "monumental cinema awash with gorgeous tones" and _[Total Film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total\_Film "Total Film")_ wrote that Yates combines "spectacle and emotion into a thrilling final chapter."[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-74)[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-75) Author J. K. Rowling remarked that "everyone who watches _Deathly Hallows – Part 2_ is going to see that he's steered us home magnificently. It's incredible."[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-76)[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-77) Part 2 is one of two _Harry Potter_ films to pass the $1 billion mark during its original theatrical run; it became the [highest-grossing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_highest-grossing_films#Highest-grossing_films "List of highest-grossing films") film in the series and the highest-grossing film of 2011, making Yates the director of the highest-grossing non-[James Cameron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Cameron "James Cameron") film of all time in August 2011.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-78)[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-79) Amongst other accolades, Yates won his second Empire Award for Best Director and joined the principal creative team of _Harry Potter_ in receiving the 2012 [ADG Award for Outstanding Contribution to Cinematic Imagery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ADG_Excellence_in_Production_Design_Award "ADG Excellence in Production Design Award") for their work on _Deathly Hallows – Part 2_ and the series in general.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-80)

Yates attended the [64th British Academy Film Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/64th_British_Academy_Film_Awards "64th British Academy Film Awards") in February 2011, where he was joined by J. K. Rowling, David Heyman, Mike Newell, Alfonso Cuarón, [David Barron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Barron_(film_producer) "David Barron (film producer)"), [Rupert Grint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rupert_Grint "Rupert Grint"), and [Emma Watson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emma_Watson "Emma Watson") in collecting the [Michael Balcon Award for Outstanding British Contribution to Cinema](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/64th_British_Academy_Film_Awards#Michael_Balcon_Award_for_Outstanding_British_Contribution_to_Cinema "64th British Academy Film Awards") on behalf of the _Harry Potter_ films. [Daniel Radcliffe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Radcliffe "Daniel Radcliffe"), who portrayed the films' titular character, commented on working with Yates, saying that he "added his own sense of grit and realism [to the series] that perhaps wasn't there so much before. I think we all had a fantastic time working with David. I know we did."[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-DavidYatesEarlyLifeBAFTA-1)[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-81)

### _Tyrant_ and _Tarzan_ (2012–2016)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=David_Yates&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Tyrant and Tarzan (2012–2016)")]

By 2012, Yates was working on a few [Warner Bros.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Bros. "Warner Bros.") projects, including a _Tarzan_ feature film and an [Al Capone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Capone "Al Capone") biopic called _Cicero_.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-82)[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-83) He also controversially said that he was working with [BBC Worldwide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_Worldwide "BBC Worldwide") on plans to develop a _[Doctor Who](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor\_Who "Doctor Who")_ film,[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-84) although this was denied by the showrunner, [Steven Moffat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Moffat "Steven Moffat"), in July 2012.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-85) Because of production delays, Yates began to explore other projects including television work.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-86)

[![Image 21](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/82/David_Yates_%2827996598333%29.jpg/250px-David_Yates_%2827996598333%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:David_Yates_(27996598333).jpg)

Yates speaking at [San Diego Comic-Con](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Diego_Comic-Con "San Diego Comic-Con"), 2016

In 2013, he returned to television by signing on to direct the [television pilot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Television_pilot "Television pilot") of _[Tyrant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tyrant\_(TV\_series) "Tyrant (TV series)")_, an American drama production set against the US–Middle East conflict.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-87) The following year, Yates began shooting _[The Legend of Tarzan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Legend\_of\_Tarzan\_(film) "The Legend of Tarzan (film)")_, starring [Alexander Skarsgård](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_Skarsg%C3%A5rd "Alexander Skarsgård"), [Samuel L. Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samuel_L._Jackson "Samuel L. Jackson"), [Margot Robbie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Margot_Robbie "Margot Robbie"), [Djimon Hounsou](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Djimon_Hounsou "Djimon Hounsou"), [Jim Broadbent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Broadbent "Jim Broadbent"), and [Christoph Waltz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christoph_Waltz "Christoph Waltz"). The film, released in 2016, opened to mixed reviews and a worldwide total of $356.7 million.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-88)

### _Fantastic Beasts_ series (2016–2022)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=David_Yates&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Fantastic Beasts series (2016–2022)")]

Yates directed _[Fantastic Beasts and Where to Find Them](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fantastic\_Beasts\_and\_Where\_to\_Find\_Them\_(film) "Fantastic Beasts and Where to Find Them (film)")_, a 2016 film which is the first in a series of five instalments based on J. K. Rowling's book, set in the world of her _Harry Potter_ novels.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-89) David Heyman and _Harry Potter_ screenwriter [Steve Kloves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Kloves "Steve Kloves") joined Yates and J. K. Rowling in developing the script.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-90) The film was released in November 2016, it received generally positive reviews and was a commercial success having grossed $814 million. It stars [Eddie Redmayne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eddie_Redmayne "Eddie Redmayne"), [Katherine Waterston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katherine_Waterston "Katherine Waterston"), [Dan Fogler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Fogler "Dan Fogler"), [Alison Sudol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alison_Sudol "Alison Sudol"), [Ezra Miller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ezra_Miller "Ezra Miller"), [Colin Farrell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colin_Farrell "Colin Farrell"), and [Johnny Depp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnny_Depp "Johnny Depp").

Yates directed the 2018 sequel, _[Fantastic Beasts: The Crimes of Grindelwald](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fantastic\_Beasts:\_The\_Crimes\_of\_Grindelwald "Fantastic Beasts: The Crimes of Grindelwald")_ which received mixed critical reception but emerged a box office success having grossed $654 million. In an interview with _The Hollywood Reporter_, he stated he was open to directing all five planned films in the _Fantastic Beasts_ series.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-91) He returned to direct the third film, _[Fantastic Beasts: The Secrets of Dumbledore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fantastic\_Beasts:\_The\_Secrets\_of\_Dumbledore "Fantastic Beasts: The Secrets of Dumbledore")_ in 2022 which also received mixed critical reception and grossed $407 million worldwide, making it a box office disappointment and the [lowest-grossing film in the Wizarding World franchise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wizarding_World "Wizarding World").

## Directorial style

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=David_Yates&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Directorial style")]

Commenting on their work on _Harry Potter_, [Emma Watson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emma_Watson "Emma Watson") stated that Yates liked to push the cast and crew to physical and emotional extremes, with [Gary Oldman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gary_Oldman "Gary Oldman") confirming Yates's preference for working slowly by shooting numerous [takes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Take "Take") to draw the finest performances out of the cast.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-97)[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-98) Yates has been influenced by such directors as [Steven Spielberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Spielberg "Steven Spielberg"), [David Lean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Lean "David Lean"), and [Ken Loach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Loach "Ken Loach").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-FilmLondon-DavidYates-10) Yates's style of work includes social and political themes, character-driven narratives, realism, and atmospheric drama.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-DavidYatesBaltimore2-99)[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-100)[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Yates#cite_note-David_Yates_RTV-101)

 Accountability and transparency are core values at the Wikimedia Foundation. We manage funds and resources to ensure that every contribution supports our mission. We have earned the Platinum Seal of Transparency from Candid (formerly GuideStar), and Charity Navigator awarded us its highest rating. 45% Investment in Technology 
Nearly half of our budget goes toward supporting the technology that powers Wikipedia and other Wikimedia projects. We are constantly working to enhance the user experience for both contributors and readers, improve site security, and ensure reliable access to our websites globally. This infrastructure and product support sustain one of the top ten most visited websites in the world, all at a fraction of the cost of popular for-profit websites.

32% Support for Volunteers 
The global reach of Wikimedia projects is made possible by the hard work of volunteers from across the globe. We provide grants, legal support, and other resources to help build vibrant volunteer communities. Additionally, we promote community engagement through outreach initiatives and advocate for the growth and protection of free knowledge.

12% Allocation to Fundraising Efforts 
Donor support is crucial to sustaining Wikipedia and our other free knowledge endeavors. Our team is committed to efficient and effective fundraising throughout the year, ensuring that every contribution helps advance our mission.

11% General and Administrative Expenses 
Operational costs are essential for the smooth management and governance of the Wikimedia Foundation. These expenses help us recruit top talent and support staff around the world, empowering them to carry out the mission of the Wikimedia Foundation.
