## Wayne Morris

This actor had a very distinguished war record followed by a pretty good career in films which was cut short by his sudden death at a very young age. In fact his film career had started well before the War but from 1941 he did not make any more until hostilities had ended and he was back in business.

[![Image 1: Marksman LC](https://fiftieswesterns.files.wordpress.com/2016/02/marksman-lc.jpg?w=500&h=382)](https://fiftieswesterns.files.wordpress.com/2016/02/marksman-lc.jpg)

**Wayne Morris**  
 (February 17, 1914 – September 14, 1959)

Warner Archive have released on DVD quite a few Wayne Morris films. He gave tremendous service to his country during World War II — seven Japanese planes shot down, five ships sunk.

Above in **_The Marksman_ (1953),** one of the Westerns Morris made for Allied Artists, which is part of Warner Archive’s Wayne Morris double feature.

One of his later appearances was in the TV Series **Bat Masterson** starring **Gene Barry.**

[![Image 2: Warner Brothers star, Wayne Morris in he 1930s](https://jnpickens.files.wordpress.com/2013/05/wayne-morris3.jpg?w=278&h=346)](https://jnpickens.files.wordpress.com/2013/05/wayne-morris3.jpg)

He can be seen playing alongside Bette Davis as a boxer in “Kid Galahad” (1937) or a cadet running amok at the Virginia Military Institute in “[Brother Rat](http://www.amazon.com/gp/offer-listing/6304288891/ref=as_li_qf_sp_asin_tl?ie=UTF8&camp=211189&creative=373493&creativeASIN=6304288891&link_code=am3&tag=comeoverholl-20).”

Wayne Morris may not be a name you’re familiar with but you have most likely seen the husky, affable blond in Warner Brothers 1930s and 1940s films.

But you may not be familiar with Morris’ war time record.  
 We frequently hear about Hollywood actors such as James Stewart, Clark Gable and Mickey Rooney who enlisted and were decorated for their bravery during World War II.

However, Wayne Morris is rarely recognised for his service and was one of World War II’s first flying aces.

His interest in flying started in Hollywood.

While filming “Flying Angles” (1940) with Jane Wyman and Dennis Morgan, Morris learned how to fly a plane.

[![Image 3: Morris in 1944 in his plane "Meatball." The decals show how many Japanese planes he shot down. ](https://jnpickens.files.wordpress.com/2013/05/wayne-1944.jpg?w=306&h=384)](https://jnpickens.files.wordpress.com/2013/05/wayne-1944.jpg)

Once World War II began, Morris joined the Naval Reserve and became a Naval flier in 1942 on the U.S.S. Essex. He put his career on hold to fight. The same year he was married to Olympic swimmer Patricia O’Rourke.

“Every time they showed a picture aboard the Essex, I was scared to death it would be one of mine,” Morris said. “That’s something I could never have lived down.”

Morris flew 57 missions-while some actors only flew 20 or less- and made seven kills, which qualified him as an ace. He also helped sink five enemy ships.

He originally was told he was too big to fly fighter planes until he went to his uncle-in-law, Cdr. David McCampbell who wrote him a letter, allowing him to fly the VF-15, according to “McCampbell’s Heroes: the Story of the U.S. Navy’s Most Celebrated Carrier Fighter of the Pacific”, Edwin P. Hoyt.

Three of his planes were so badly damaged by enemy fire that they were deemed unfit to fly and were dumped in the ocean, according to IMDB.

“As to what a fellow thinks when he’s scared, I guess it’s the same with anyone. You get fleeting glimpses in your mind of your home, your wife, the baby you want to see,” Morris said. “You see so clearly all the mistakes you made. You want another chance to correct those mistakes. You wonder how you could have attached so much importance to ridiculous, meaningless things in your life. But before you get to thinking too much, you’re off into action and everything else is forgotten.”

For his duty, Morris was honoured with four Distinguished Flying Crosses and two Air Medals.

When he returned to Hollywood after four year at war, his once promising career floundered and Warner Brothers did not allow him to act for a year.

[![Image 4: Jack Warner welcoming actors home from the war in 1945 including Wayne Morris, Ronald Reagan, Army Air Forces; Jack Warner; Gig Young, Coast Guard; and Harry Lewis, Army.](https://jnpickens.files.wordpress.com/2013/05/wayne-morris.jpg?w=584)](https://jnpickens.files.wordpress.com/2013/05/wayne-morris.jpg)

Morris’s most notable post-war films include “**[The Voice of the Turtle](http://www.amazon.com/gp/offer-listing/B00A1AU6VC/ref=as_li_qf_sp_asin_tl?ie=UTF8&camp=211189&creative=373493&creativeASIN=B00A1AU6VC&link_code=am3&tag=comeoverholl-20),”** “**[John Loves Mary](http://www.amazon.com/gp/offer-listing/B002EAYE1K/ref=as_li_qf_sp_asin_tl?ie=UTF8&camp=211189&creative=373493&creativeASIN=B002EAYE1K&link_code=am3&tag=comeoverholl-20)”** and “**[Paths of Glory](http://www.amazon.com/gp/offer-listing/B001BO5B6C/ref=as_li_qf_sp_asin_tl?ie=UTF8&camp=211189&creative=373493&creativeASIN=B001BO5B6C&link_code=am3&tag=comeoverholl-20).”** His career ended with several B-westerns.

At the age of 45, Morris passed away in 1959 from a massive heart attack.

But his service to his country was not forgotten. Morris is buried in Arlington Cemetery and was given full military honors at his funeral.

[![Image 5: Morris with his wife Patricia and daughter Pamela in 1946.](https://jnpickens.files.wordpress.com/2013/05/wayne-morris2.jpg?w=231&h=300)](https://jnpickens.files.wordpress.com/2013/05/wayne-morris2.jpg)

Before he started out in Hollywood, he played football at Los Angeles Junior College and worked as a forest ranger.

  - **Occupations:** Real‑estate developer, planner and founder of the town of **Reston, Virginia**.  
  - **Education:** Horace Mann School; Harvard University.  
  - **Military Service:** U.S. Army, World War II, officer’s candidate school; served in Paris and Belgium.  
  - **Family:** Married four times. Had one son and one daughter from his first marriage (daughter’s name not provided in this article). Survived by wife **Cheryl Terio Simon**, daughter, and several step‑children.  

- **Town of Reston, Virginia**  
  - Conceptualized in 1961 when Simon purchased 6,750 acres of farmland in Fairfax County.  
  - Design of the new town was carried out by the firm **Conklin + Rossant**.  
  - Construction and development of the town began in 1964; Simon directed its planning and construction during the 1960s.  
  - Reston was named after Simon’s initials (RES) and envisioned as a “new town” community where people could live, work and play without long commutes.  

- **Additional Notes from Article**  
  - Simon lived in a condo at **Heron House** overlooking Lake Anne at the time of his death.  
  - He met his final wife, Cheryl, aboard a high‑rise elevator.  
  - The Reston Town Center and various village centers were built per his original mixed‑use vision.
